commits.author: usavsolutionsinc
commits.subject: feat(support): link many STNs to one ticket, from outbound and support
commits.body:
A ticket routinely concerns several shipping tracking numbers (split
shipments, re-ships, multi-box claims), but UNIQUE (organization_id,
zendesk_ticket_id) gave it exactly ONE entity slot — many-STN was
physically impossible, not merely un-surfaced. Outbound had zero link UI;
support had one control gated `!tracking`, so it vanished the moment any
tracking resolved — exactly the wall a second STN hits.

Model: solve it inside ticket_links using the pattern shipment_links already
invented — many rows + a PARTIAL unique index, so the invariant is enforced
by an index rather than by convention. The one-entity rule is narrowed, not
removed: from "one ROW per ticket" to "one ANCHOR per ticket" (what the
ticket is about), with any number of references (other entities it touches).

  ux_ticket_links_ticket_entity (org, ticket, entity_type, entity_id)
  ux_ticket_links_ticket_anchor (org, ticket) WHERE link_role='anchor'

Rejected shipment_links owner_type='SUPPORT_TICKET': it breaks under
promotion — promoteShipmentTicketToReceiving rewrites the anchor to a carton
the many-list never heard of, with no FK and nothing to detect the drift.
link_role over a boolean follows photo_entity_links.link_role, the house's
own second-discriminator-axis precedent (and Jira's issuelinktype).

Migrations (ordering is load-bearing):
- 2026-07-16   is_primary + both unique indexes + org-led index + STN
               parent-delete trigger. Pure no-op: while every row is an
               anchor, old and new uniques are strictly equivalent.
- 2026-07-16b  link_role + bidirectional sync trigger (expand/contract — a
               hard swap has a broken window in BOTH orderings; the trigger
               makes migration and deploy independent).
- 2026-07-16c  drops the legacy unique. THIS is what turns the feature on,
               and it could only be written after the replacement code was
               live: the old code upserted ON CONFLICT (org, ticket), and
               dropping that under it fails every link.

Also fixes, found on the way:
- The link waist never called recordAudit at all (route-skeleton violation).
- Timeline link moments now come from ops_events, not ticket_links row
  state — which cannot express a detach, leaving 'unlinked' dead code.
  audit_logs was wrong: it's admin-gated, so invisible to the operators
  doing the linking. Receiving stays on row state (107 rows of history);
  shipment had zero, so it loses nothing by moving.
- promoteShipmentTicketToReceiving now filters is_primary — without it a
  ticket that merely references an STN gets yanked onto a carton.
- Outbound threads showed no linked ticket at all; extracted the RECEIVING
  branch's lookup so ORDER shares it, querying both anchor conventions.
- LinkageStrip's POST switched anchor→reference; ungating alone would have
  moved the wall from "control hidden" to "409 on click".
- Promoted TicketPicker/useTicketSearch to a shared home; receiving composes
  them. LinkCandidate is now an alias of TicketCandidate (they were
  structurally identical, which had forced an unsafe cast).

Verified: two STNs on one ticket, second anchor rejected by the partial
unique, proven against the real schema and rolled back. npm run verify green
(8/8). E2E 3/3 on the route; unbox context proves an STN-only link resolves
on the carton with no RECEIVING link, plus the negative control.

Not verified: any UI renders — both UI specs are red/skipped on selectors
and fixtures, not code. See docs/todo/ticket-stn-many-link-plan.md for that
and the ranked follow-ups (re-key on support_ticket_id is #1: internal
tickets cannot be linked at all today).

commits.author: usavsolutionsinc
commits.subject: fix(receiving-claim): surface real field error + bulletproof NAS archive validation
commits.body:
The "Back up to NAS" form and the filed-ticket dropdown Archive button both
POST to /api/receiving/zendesk-claim/archive-only. Its Zod schema rejected the
request and the client only showed `error` ("Validation failed"), swallowing
the `details` that name the actual field — so the failure was undiagnosable in
prod.

Root cause on the carton/chip path: receiving/line ids arrive as bigint-
serialized strings, and `z.coerce.number()` turns "" / null into 0, which then
fails `.positive()` (nullable only catches real null). An empty lineId on a
carton-level archive tripped this.

- archive-only route: safeParse (not .parse) → log the exact payload +

commits.author: usavsolutionsinc
commits.subject: Make receiving idempotent against retries + concurrent double-fire (BUG-0013/0014)
commits.body:
BUG-0013: receiveLineUnits now short-circuits on a batch-level idempotency
guard — if this client_event_id's per-unit events already exist on the line
(committed by a prior call), return the current state without mutating. The old
per-unit ordinal suffix (`:unit-N`, N from the moving quantity_received) shifted
on retry, so ON CONFLICT(client_event_id) missed and the counter + non-serial
ledger double-applied; only mark-received-po's qty clamp masked it. Now
idempotent for any caller; concurrent dups block on the FOR UPDATE lock then
short-circuit.

BUG-0014: add reserve-up-front idempotency (claimOrReplay / finalize /
release) so two concurrent requests with the same Idempotency-Key can't both
run produce() (which double-called Zoho purchase-receive). The first claims a
pending row; a concurrent second replays the finished response or gets 409
in-progress. Abandoned claims self-heal after a stale window. Additive — the
existing get/save helpers are unchanged (zero blast radius on the other ~34
routes); adopted in mark-received-po at its existing claim/finalize/catch spots.
DB-free unit test covers proceed/replay/in-progress/stale-reclaim/release/5xx.

The matched-order and not-found paths wrote the PACK_COMPLETED audit row
with the shared `pool` connection while the station_activity_logs row was
created on the open withTenantTransaction `client`. The uncommitted SAL row
wasn't visible to the separate connection, so the
audit_logs.station_activity_log_id FK violated (23503) and rolled back the
whole pack — surfacing as a 500 on POST /api/packing-logs.

Switch both calls to recordAudit(client, ctx, req, …): runs in the same
transaction (FK resolves) and never throws (audit failures are logged and
dropped), so a future audit hiccup can't roll back a completed pack. Keeps
the historical uppercase entityType literals to preserve audit-dashboard
continuity; action uses AUDIT_ACTION.PACK_COMPLETED (identical value).

(the executor path only uses .query) — removes the unsafe cast in parts-sort and
lets any caller thread a partial tx client without one. Backward-compatible: a
full PoolClient still satisfies the narrower type.

commits.subject: fix(workflow): applyTransition idempotency must not swallow expectedFrom drift
commits.body:
transition() runs the expectedFrom drift check BEFORE the guard's identity
check, so with optimistic concurrency a 409 — even one where from===to — is a
drift rejection the caller asked to fail on, not an idempotent re-entry. Only
treat from===to as an idempotent re-entry when no expectedFrom was supplied;
otherwise surface the 409 (no event, no tap). recordTestVerdict doesn't use
expectedFrom, so this is a latent-edge hardening for future callers + a test.

coverage so legitimate verdicts never 409.

commits.subject: feat(workflow): unpark/recovery path for stuck items (Phase 1.0)
commits.body:
advanceItem() parks units as blocked (await) or error (throw/unknown type),
but nothing reset them — errored units silently died. Adds the recovery path:

- recoverItem() (src/lib/workflow/recover.ts): tenant-scoped reset of one
  blocked|error item_workflow_state row back to active. Writes an
  inventory_events NOTE (timeline) + a workflow_runs 'unpark' row (engine log),
  then a best-effort emitWorkflowEvent so the Live lens refetches. Leaves
  serial_units.current_status untouched — only the engine's position was stuck.
- POST /api/studio/items/[id]/recover — HTTP shell + formal audit row
  (action 'workflow.item.recover' as a string literal; no audit-logs constant
  churn while that file is mid-edit by concurrent work).
- GET  /api/studio/items/stuck — the per-item triage feed (blocked|error) the
  Live lens only counts in aggregate.
- New permission studio.recover (non-destructive, no step-up: a re-park is one
  scan away) so a floor lead can unpark without graph-edit rights.

Manifest regen (docs/security/route-permissions.json) is left to the owning
audit-route-auth:emit flow (concurrently mid-regen), not bundled here.

commits.author: DENSENSE8
commits.subject: feat(workflow): real per-unit AdvanceLock replacing NULL_LOCK (Phase 1.0)
commits.body:
Best-effort Upstash Redis mutex keyed wf:advance:{serialUnitId}, wired into
the production advance() path. Mirrors api-guard.ts's REST /pipeline shape.

Failure policy (the lock narrows races; engine idempotency is the backstop):
- Redis unconfigured -> acquire() true / release() no-op (== NULL_LOCK), so
  dev/CI/preview are unaffected.
- SET NX miss (already held) -> acquire() false -> 2nd concurrent advance noops.
- Redis error/timeout -> acquire() true (fail OPEN), never stalls a tap.

Short TTL auto-expires a crashed holder; release is a token-checked
compare-and-delete (Lua) so we never free a lock a later advance re-acquired.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: DENSENSE8
commits.subject: feat(tenancy): make serial_units writer org-required + FORCE RLS migration
commits.body:
upsertSerialUnit now takes a REQUIRED orgId: the unscoped SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE
branches and the raw-pool dispatcher are deleted, so the canonical writer always
stamps organization_id (or sets app.current_org on an external client). This
removes the FORCE-RLS footgun (relying on the column default, which loud-fails
without the GUC) and the latent cross-tenant FOR UPDATE lock bug.

syncTsnToSerialUnit / syncSkuToSerialUnit also require orgId. Threaded callers:
post-multi-sn, mark-received (ctx.organizationId), receive-line
(input.organizationId), serial-attach attachSerialToLine (now requires orgId,
legacy raw-pool path removed) + its route callers scan-serial and
mark-received-po, and the serials route. recordUnitEvent (test-only) gains
organizationId on its input.

Adds 2026-06-20b_enforce_tenant_isolation_serial_units.sql (FORCE phase E) and
scripts/verify-serial-units-force.mjs (app_tenant baseline -> apply -> reread ->
auto-relax harness). Apply ONLY after this code deploys.
